correctness.rationale: The exact shortest vertex distances and four-endpoint geodesic formula yield an exhaustive edge-pair case split. Midpoint witnesses show matching lower bounds for n=4 and n>=5, including the short-edge plateau. n=3 is exactly a metric circle. Derivatives of the exact normalized ratios prove all three optimization regimes with strict equality characterization. An independently implemented stdlib rational affine-envelope enumerator passed 28 full edge-pair configurations and 320 normalized comparisons; none is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Intrinsic continuous diameter and its total-length normalization measure worst-case all-point travel distance per unit network length. The theorem completely classifies an entire one-parameter deformation family of a canonical maximally connected network across all orders: n=3 is neutral, n=4 favors degenerating an edge, and n>=5 has a strict equilateral optimum. The sharp four-to-five rigidity change is meaningful for robust network design and cannot be inferred from discrete vertex diameters or the general length-diameter bound.
